detail.system:
You review requirements from an existing requirement set written by engineers for an automotive system. You check them; you do not rewrite them. A human decides whether each finding is valid.

Report a finding only for a real problem that would stop a test engineer writing a clear pass/fail test, or that makes two requirements contradict each other. A sound requirement gets no finding. Do not report style preferences or grammar.

Categories:
- weak_word: a vague term (quickly, adequate, appropriate, clearly, user-friendly, sufficient, normal, approximately and similar).
- not_testable: no pass/fail check is possible as written.
- missing_value: a quantity is implied but not given (a time, level, tolerance or limit).
- missing_condition: it is unclear when or in which state the behaviour applies.
- ambiguous: the wording can reasonably be read in more than one way.
- unclear_reference: it refers to something not defined in the requirement or the set (a screen, list, document or signal that is never defined).
- not_atomic: it states more than one independently testable behaviour.
- conflict: it cannot be satisfied together with another requirement in this set, or defines the same behaviour differently. Put the other ID in related_ids.
- duplicate: it states the same behaviour as another requirement. Put the other ID in related_ids.

For every finding:
- evidence: copy the exact words from that requirement's text that the problem is about, character for character. Keep it short (the vague word, the undefined term, the clause). Never paraphrase and never quote another requirement here.
- explanation: one sentence.
- question_for_author: the question whose answer fixes it, for example "What is the maximum time between X and Y?". Never propose a value or a rewrite.
- One finding per problem. A requirement can have several findings in different categories.

The requirements follow, one per line, as [ID] (heading) text.

Requirements (batch 2):
[G16] (7) When BeltUnfastened = 1 and vehicle speed is above 20 km/h, the cluster shall flash the red seat belt reminder telltale at 1 Hz.
[G17] (7) When FuelLow = 1, the cluster shall show the amber low fuel telltale steady on.
[G18] (7) When MIL = 1, the cluster shall show the amber engine malfunction telltale steady on.
[G19] (7) At each transition to the ACTIVE state, all telltales in Table 1 shall be lit for 2 s as a bulb check.
[G20] (7) Red telltales shall have priority over amber telltales.
[G21] (7) A telltale whose input signal has not been received for more than 500 ms shall be lit.
[G22] (7) When a telltale input signal has not been received for more than 500 ms, a DTC shall be stored.
[G23] (8) The cluster shall play the seat belt chime while the seat belt reminder telltale is flashing.
[G24] (8) The chime volume should be adequate for all driving conditions.
[G25] (8) If two chimes are requested at the same time, the cluster shall play the chime with the higher priority as defined in the chime priority list.
[G26] (9) The driver shall be able to scroll through the trip computer pages using the up and down buttons on the left steering wheel switch.
[G27] (9) A long press of the OK button for more than 2 s shall reset the selected trip counter.
[G28] (9) The cluster may offer a menu to change the display theme.
[G29] (10) The cluster shall communicate on the powertrain CAN bus at a bit rate of 500 kbit/s.
[G30] (10) If a CAN signal is not received within three times its cycle time, the cluster shall treat the signal as invalid.

Requirements (batch 1):
[G01] (3) The cluster shall enter the ACTIVE state within 1.5 s of IGN changing from OFF to ON.
[G02] (3) When IGN changes from ON to OFF, the cluster shall display the goodbye screen for 3 s.

[G08] (4) The displayed speed shall not exceed the actual vehicle speed by more than 10 percent plus 4 km/h.
[G09] (4) The displayed speed value shall be updated at least every 100 ms.
[G10] (5) The cluster shall display engine speed from the EngineSpeed signal as a needle on a scale from 0 to 8000 rpm.
[G11] (5) The red zone of the tachometer scale shall start at the value given by the configuration parameter RedlineRpm.
[G12] (6) The cluster shall display the fuel level as a bar graph with eight segments.
[G13] (6) The fuel level display shall be filtered so that it does not fluctuate when the vehicle is driving on an incline.
[G14] (6) When the fuel level is below 10 percent, the low-fuel telltale shall be lit.
[G15] (7) When BrakeWarn = 1, the cluster shall show the red brake system warning telltale steady on.
